_description: Curated PDB structures and AutoDock Vina docking grids for 12 untargeted lupus genes (10 validated + 2 AlphaFold models needing grid refinement). Grid centers based on co-crystallized ligand coordinates or catalytic site residues. Grid boxes sized for small-molecule docking (20-25Å per dimension).
_instructions: To refine grid boxes: open the PDB in PyMOL/Chimera, select the co-crystallized ligand, and run `get_center_of_mass sele` for center. Adjust grid_size to cover the binding pocket plus ~5Å padding. Targets with grid_validated=false are skipped by the docking engine — set grid_center to non-null coordinates to enable docking.

BLK.binding_site: ATP-binding pocket (kinase hinge region between N-lobe and C-lobe)
BLK.notes: Src-family kinase. Active conformation with DFG-in. The ATP analog occupies the hinge region (residues M85-E91). Grid centered on the adenine ring of ANP.

IRAK4.notes: Key kinase downstream of MYD88 in TLR7/TLR9 signaling. Co-crystallized with a clinical-stage inhibitor. High-quality structure for SBVS.

PTPN22.binding_site: Catalytic phosphatase pocket (P-loop: C227-R233, WPD-loop: D195-P199)
PTPN22.notes: Lymphoid tyrosine phosphatase (LYP). Catalytic site contains conserved C227. Grid centered on the P-loop/catalytic cysteine. Apo structure — no bound inhibitor.

TNFAIP3.binding_site: OTU domain deubiquitinase catalytic pocket (C103, H256, D272 catalytic triad)
TNFAIP3.notes: A20 OTU domain. Negative regulator of NF-κB. Catalytic triad defines the active site pocket. Grid centered on the catalytic cysteine C103. Apo structure.

TLR7.binding_site: Ligand-binding pocket in the leucine-rich repeat (LRR) solenoid (between LRR11-LRR14)
TLR7.notes: Cryo-EM structure of TLR7-UNC93B1 complex. CL097 binds in the hydrophobic pocket between LRR11-LRR14. Moderate resolution; use flexible sidechain docking if possible. Key SLE target — gain-of-function mutations cause lupus.

TLR9.binding_site: Predicted ligand-binding pocket (LRR solenoid, homologous to TLR7 LRR11-LRR14 region)
TLR9.notes: ⚠️ ALPHAFOLD MODEL — GRID NOT VALIDATED. The docking engine will skip this target until grid_center is set (set grid_center to non-null coordinates). No high-resolution experimental structure of full-length TLR9 with inhibitor available. Use the AlphaFold model with caution; consider blind docking or use the TLR7 structure (7CYN) as a homology template for grid definition. Detectable binding pocket predicted between LRR11-LRR14 (homologous to TLR7).

FCGR2A.binding_site: IgG Fc-binding interface (BC loop, C'E loop, FG loop of the D2 domain)
FCGR2A.notes: FcγRIIa (CD32a). Structure is the FcγRIIa-Fc complex. The Fc-binding interface involves the BC, C'E, and FG loops of the D2 domain. Grid centered on the IgG-binding groove. Targeting the Fc-binding interface may modulate immune complex signaling. Apo receptor chain used for docking grid.

FCGR3A.binding_site: IgG Fc-binding interface (D2 domain, membrane-proximal region)
FCGR3A.notes: FcγRIIIa (CD16a) ectodomain. Grid centered on the Fc-binding loops. V158F polymorphism in this gene alters IgG affinity and SLE risk.

ITGAM.binding_site: I-domain metal ion-dependent adhesion site (MIDAS motif: D239, T240, S242)
ITGAM.notes: Integrin αM I-domain (CD11b). The MIDAS motif coordinates Mg²⁺ and mediates ligand binding. Grid centered on the MIDAS metal ion site. SLE-associated R77H mutation is in the β-propeller domain (not in this structure — this is the I-domain only).

MYD88.binding_site: TIR domain BB-loop (residues 195-210) — critical for TLR TIR:MyD88 TIR homotypic interaction
MYD88.notes: MyD88 TIR domain. BB-loop is the key protein-protein interaction site with TLR7/TLR9 TIR domains. Targeting this PPI interface could disrupt TLR→MyD88 signaling. Grid centered on the BB-loop (critical for Myddosome assembly).

TNFSF4.binding_site: Predicted receptor-binding interface (TNF homology domain, trimer interface)
TNFSF4.notes: ⚠️ ALPHAFOLD MODEL — GRID NOT VALIDATED. The docking engine will skip this target until grid_center is set (set grid_center to non-null coordinates). OX40L (TNFSF4). No inhibitor-bound crystal structure available. The TNF homology domain (THD) forms a trimer and binds OX40 receptor. Target the receptor-binding interface or trimer interface.

UBE2L3.binding_site: Catalytic cysteine pocket (C86) — E2 ubiquitin-conjugating active site
UBE2L3.notes: UBCH7 E2 enzyme (chain D in the UBE2L3-CBL complex). The catalytic cysteine C86 defines the active site. Grid centered on the catalytic cysteine pocket. ⚠️ Verify these coordinates against the actual PDB — the grid center (42.5, 8.1, 12.3) may need adjustment based on the specific crystal lattice. Targeting the E2 active site could modulate ubiquitination and NF-κB activation in B cells.

excluded_targets.reason: MHC class II protein complex — presents peptide antigens. No small-molecule binding pocket suitable for conventional docking. While alleles are strongly associated with SLE (OR 2.5), the protein functions via peptide presentation to TCRs, not via a druggable catalytic site.

Transcription factor. The DNA-binding domain (PDB: 3DSH) has a shallow DNA-binding interface, not a deep small-molecule pocket. Targeting IRF5 requires protein-protein or protein-DNA interface disruption — beyond the scope of standard Vina docking.

Transcription factor. Similar to IRF5 — the DNA-binding domain lacks a conventional small-molecule binding pocket. Master regulator of type I IFN production but not currently druggable by small molecules.

Scaffold protein with ankyrin repeats. Functions via protein-protein interactions (e.g., with IP3R and Lyn). No known small-molecule binding site. No high-resolution structure of the full-length protein available.

Transcription factor (BLIMP-1). Zinc finger domains mediate DNA binding but lack deep druggable pockets. No inhibitor-bound structures available. Critical for plasma cell differentiation but not yet druggable.

Ubiquitin-binding adaptor protein (ABIN-1). Functions via ubiquitin-binding domains interacting with polyubiquitin chains and A20. No deep small-molecule binding pocket. No high-resolution full-length structure available.

Engulfment and cell motility protein. Large multi-domain scaffold that functions via protein-protein interactions. No defined small-molecule binding pocket. No high-resolution full-length structure available.

Core autophagy protein. Functions as part of the ATG12-ATG5-ATG16L1 E3-like ligase complex via protein-protein interactions. No conventional small-molecule binding pocket. Structure known (PDB: 1T06) but not druggable by standard docking.

Complement protein. Functions as part of the C1 complex (C1q-C1r-C1s). Collagen-like and globular domains mediate pattern recognition. No small-molecule binding pocket — C1q initiates complement via multivalent binding to antibody Fc regions and CRP.

Complement serine protease zymogen. C2 circulates as an inactive proenzyme. The catalytic site is only formed after C1s-mediated cleavage and incorporation into the C3 convertase complex (C4b2a) — the active site cannot be docked against in isolation. Even though serine proteases are generally druggable, C2's activation mechanism requires the full C4b-C2a complex context, making isolated C2 docking structurally meaningless. Complement C1s inhibitors (e.g., sutimlimab) demonstrate that targeting upstream complement proteases is feasible, but C2 specifically lacks the structural biology data needed for reliable docking.

Complement protein. Functions via covalent attachment to target surfaces (thioester bond). The thioester is buried in the native protein and only exposed upon C1s cleavage. Not a conventional enzymatic target. Structural studies exist but no small-molecule binding pocket.

No experimental SH2 domain structure available. Only the N-terminal domain and coiled-coil domain (PDB: 4NUI, 4NUJ at 2.5Å) have been crystallized for STAT4. These domains lack the phosphotyrosine-binding SH2 domain that mediates STAT4 dimerization. STAT1/STAT3 SH2 domain structures (e.g., 1BGF) could serve as homology templates but are not STAT4-specific and would require careful model building. The SH2 domain remains an attractive theoretical target (blocking dimerization could suppress Th1/Th17-driven autoimmunity), but reliable docking requires a STAT4-specific SH2 domain structure.

targeted_genes_for_validation.notes: VALIDATION TARGET — already targeted by baricitinib/tofacitinib. Use as a positive control for docking pipeline validation. High-resolution (1.33Å) structure with bound inhibitor. Dock baricitinib (SMILES available) and verify it ranks highly.

targeted_genes_for_validation.binding_site: ATP-binding pocket (kinase domain, Cys481 covalent targeting site)
targeted_genes_for_validation.notes: VALIDATION TARGET — already targeted by acalabrutinib. Use as a positive control. Dock acalabrutinib (SMILES available) and verify it ranks highly.

targeted_genes_for_validation.binding_site: ATP-binding pocket (JH1 kinase domain, pseudokinase JH2 domain distinct binding site)
targeted_genes_for_validation.notes: VALIDATION TARGET (negative control for domain specificity) — already targeted by deucravacitinib, which binds the JH2 pseudokinase domain, NOT the JH1 kinase domain. 6PW8 is the JH1 kinase domain structure. Docking deucravacitinib into JH1 should yield poor scores (validating that the pipeline correctly distinguishes domain specificity). For positive validation, source a TYK2 JH2 pseudokinase domain structure and dock deucravacitinib there.
